fresh_checks.checked_reasoning: The scalar is defined in the ordinary class of the fixed genuine smaller-background model. Bounded positive densities are in every finite Lp; scalar uniqueness does not assert potential uniqueness.

Strict scalar comparison with every constant translate proves that B decreases with F; B(F+a)=B(F)-a gives the uniform Lipschitz bound. Smooth gauge transport preserves the currents and the ordinary class.
The mixed-product density inequality for a convex combination of same-type potentials gives the geometric-mean subsolution. Strict comparison rules out a smaller critical scalar and proves concavity.

Common logarithmic bounds bound the scalars and densities. Relative solution bounds, L1 compactness and dominated capacity identification give the limiting equation; unique scalars identify every cluster.

The finite convex directional derivative of -B admits a Hahn--Banach minorant. Order makes it positive and constant translations give mass one. Riesz representation and closed inequalities give a compact convex supporting set.
Continuous cutoffs of compact volume-null sets and bounded L1 scalar continuity force zero support mass there. Inner regularity gives absolute continuity on all Borel sets.

Uniform test convergence preserves every supporting inequality. Right derivatives of B are minus the maximum support integral, and left derivatives minus the minimum. Singleton supports characterize Gateaux differentiability, not Frechet differentiability.

Widths in a fixed direction are upper semicontinuous by compactness. A finite concave function on a line has only countably many derivative jumps. The countable dense family and Baire argument give exactly the singleton-support residual set.
The previously proved smooth scalar derivative identifies the support with the Gauduchon adjoint probability on all continuous tests. In dimension one Stokes gives the explicit Gibbs expression.

A supporting probability alone does not identify a weak cofactor operator. The scalar-multiple product identification and compatibility with approximation remain requirements; continuous-density uniqueness remains explicitly unresolved.
H is a supremum of affine weakly continuous functions and is bounded below by B(0). The supporting inequality gives equality in the dual minimum exactly on supporting probabilities.

Large fixed cutoff amplitudes and small support volume bound all masses on small Borel sets uniformly. Finite dual sublevels are weakly compact, absolutely continuous and uniformly integrable; this yields weak L1 testing against bounded measurable functions.

Bounded continuous approximation preserves B and integrals against a fixed absolutely continuous support. Fixed dual sublevels give uniform integrability for moving supports, so bounded L1 tests pass in the minimizing identity. Infinite-H measures have objective infinity.

For singular measures, compact-null-set cutoffs make the variational supremum infinite. For densities, clipped logarithms and continuous approximations recover entropy, including infinity, with the integrable negative part controlled by h log h >= -1/e.

Closed ordinary-type mass invariance gives B=log(m)-log(Z) and the Gibbs support. Hence H=log(m)+Ent. Changing volume by e^a shifts H and entropy by the same integral; the nonclosed case is not assigned this equality.

The lower-density theorem yields the q-scaled logarithmic partition lower bound. The normalized Gauduchon trace estimate yields the n-scaled upper bound. Taking convex duals gives finite H exactly for finite entropy, with comparable sublevel bounds.

Bounds on actual equation masses imply the two inequalities for H-Ent. Gibbs probabilities and smooth adjoint probabilities give the reverse sharpness; bounded-potential regularization is a retained preceding input. Infinite endpoint cases are handled explicitly.

The smaller-background condition supplies uniform lower-density constants. Comparison with a larger Hermitian background supplies the upper bound. Common epsilon and test bounds give uniform entropy and integrability, without identifying a changing reference limit.

Ordinary singularity order and strict domination order the scalars and duals. Mixing the smaller-background reference with a bounded critical solution gives the (1-epsilon)^n lower scalar factor, valid on common finite levels.

The continuous-test uniform distance equals the finite-entropy dual distance by the attained minimum formula, in both directions. Bounded L1 approximation extends the bound to measurable tests. This is a pseudometric and does not separate singularity types.

A moving support is a 2-delta approximate minimizer for the fixed reference. Fixed dual sublevels give uniform integrability; weak L1 passage and lower semicontinuity identify the limiting support. Small-reference epsilons imply this functional convergence.

At a maximum or minimum of u_prime-(1+-epsilon)u, the corresponding Hermitian forms are ordered. Determinant comparison yields uniform logarithmic scalar bounds; bounded L1 approximation passes them to all bounded tests.

Uniform scalar and dual distance bounds place moving supports in a fixed dual sublevel and make them approximate minimizers. Uniform integrability permits bounded L1 forcing convergence and identifies the fixed-background support.

The scalar direction removes the adjoint obstruction and mean normalization removes the constant kernel, so the smooth Monge--Ampere derivative is invertible. The implicit function theorem gives smooth parameter convergence; integration of the scalar derivative reconstructs B from B(0) and its smooth adjoints.

Removing the exact divisorial current gives a bounded residual beta-psh representative. Bounds extend over divisors by submean and upper semicontinuity. Locality off the divisor and zero analytic-set mass of the bounded product identify the extended measures and transfer scalar and potential uniqueness.

Convergent sections and positive weights have a common Hessian lower bound, uniform upper bound and a common finite point. Compactness and local uniform convergence off the limiting divisor identify every L1 cluster. Hartogs bounds the suprema above, evaluation at a finite maximizing point bounds them below.

In the stated closed big model domain, positive ordinary mass supplies the earlier existence hypothesis. The classical prescribed-type uniqueness is explicitly retained as external input. Integrating the equation gives the functional and the exact logarithmic mass distance.

Projective divisors have mass (1-t)^n and distinct multiplier ideals for sufficiently large weights. Their full residual solutions have distinct distributional Hessians despite equal scalar functions. In the nonclosed example every divisor has the same positive residual e^f omega; injectivity of wedge with omega^(n-1) proves nonclosedness.

Scalar subsolution order and homogeneity give lattice order and norm homogeneity. The weighted average of critical potentials gives the triangle inequality through local Minkowski and exhaustion. The strict-barrier lower scalar estimate gives L^(nq) continuity and the density-root Holder estimate.

Hahn--Banach gives a norming L^(ell-prime) functional; taking its absolute value preserves norming at the nonnegative root. The domination bound gives weak compactness in the reflexive space. Weighted arithmetic-geometric mean proves logarithmic convexity of the exponential norm curve.

Jensen puts each positive norming functional in P_f. Conversely the exponential directional derivative bounds the probability functional on ar. Density in the weighted Lell space gives a positive extension, chosen zero where a=0; lattice domination extends it to all functions and identifies every support.

Holder bounds the weighted moment by Cq/A times the Lell norm. A constant norm along an exponential perturbation gives integral exponential <=1 and hence integral z<=0. Uniform qpsh finite moments and q

Exponential comparison gives psi<=w_lambda. The norm identity for its actual equation gives every support integral <=0. One such probability and the uniform weighted moment bound bound sup(w_lambda). The prior compactness theorem and these scalar bounds give local uniform and L1 precompactness of the centered family.

Pointwise subsolution suprema are finite by comparison and constant shifts. The mixed-product geometric-mean inequality proves concavity in forcing; translation and order give the Lipschitz bound. A supporting functional for -lambda times the envelope is a probability without requiring attainment.

Normalized critical forcing solutions place every weak cluster of forcing probabilities in P_f. Increasing continuous approximation to -lambda s proves integrability and the pointwise comparison for every selection competitor. Local product continuity identifies the cluster equation; dominated convergence gives its integral constraints. Portmanteau for bounded-above qpsh competitors proves greatestness and uniqueness of the selected cluster.

The norming-face representation makes integration of the selected potential weakly continuous, so the maximum is attained and equals zero by greatestness. Normalized compactness identifies every scalar cluster with sup(w). The preceding stronger compactness topologies give convergence of differences and local Holder convergence without asserting uniqueness of all critical solutions.

additional_open_research_occurrences.topic: Uniqueness of supporting probabilities at continuous Hermitian and general singular-reference densities
additional_open_research_occurrences.exact_source_line: Thus for a continuous $F$ in the Hermitian case, smooth approximations $F_j\to F$ uniformly produce Gauduchon adjoint probabilities whose weak cluster points all belong to $\mathcal A_0(F)$ and are absolutely continuous. If $\mathcal A_0(F)$ is a singleton, the weak limit is independent of this approximation. In particular this holds at every $F\in\mathscr U_0$. Uniqueness at every continuous density remains unresolved in this Hermitian setting, and likewise for the general singular references considered above.
additional_open_research_occurrences.inventory_relationship: The Hermitian zero-reference clause is an expository occurrence of conjecture conj:continuous-gaud-adjoint; the general singular-reference extension is broader. No new numbered problem or equivalence is claimed.

additional_open_research_occurrences.topic: Weak cofactor-current identification and compatibility with approximation
additional_open_research_occurrences.exact_source_line: A weak linearized operator requires more than a supporting probability. In this Hermitian zero-reference setting, \cref{thm:gaud-current-all-adjoints} represents each supporting probability by a determinant-weighted positive $\ddc$-closed current. Identifying that current with a scalar multiple of the weak power $\omega_u^{n-1}$ requires a justified product and compatibility with approximation.
additional_open_research_occurrences.inventory_relationship: An explicit unresolved product/approximation requirement in this chapter, not a separately numbered conjecture. No assertion that every restricted case is open in the literature.
